maria: Quick datapoint - after the 3.14 runtime merge we saw a ~18% tail-latency regress on TP inference for seq_len=2048. Profiling points to all-reduce stalls during KV cache refresh. Anyone else see this?

devin: yeah saw that on dedicated cluster-4, mainly when batch sizes are small and we hit many tiny all-reduces.

kai: can you paste the flamegraph snippet? is this ring algorithm or tree?

maria: pasting nsys trace snippet (filtered):
```
Timestamp  GPU0     GPU1     Comm
1.234s     compute  compute  ncclAllReduce (12KB)
1.237s     idle     idle     ncclAllReduce (12KB)
1.245s     compute  compute  ncclAllReduce (24KB)
```
Looks like lots of sub-20KB reductions.

liam: small message sizes will kill ring perf - latency per op dominated by startup. Tree/hierarchical may help once you have a bigger fan-in.

maria: agreed. I ran a quick microbenchmark switching NCCL_COLLNET and NCCL_TREE env flags. Results: ring baseline 1.0x, tree ~0.78x latency for 8 GPUs at 12KB messages. But for 256KB messages tree lost to ring (1.1x).

devin: interesting. Where does kernel selection come in? Are we getting fragmentation so actual comm messages are split because tensors are non-contiguous?

kai: yep. Our tensor layout in TP stage 2 does strided gathers before reduce; that generates multiple small fragments. Batch packing heuristic used to keep latency low ends up creating many tiny tensors.

maria: experiment notes I pushed to the bench branch: 
- change batching to prefer coalescing adjacent KV updates up to 128KB
- collapse small fragments at gather time (memcpy -> contiguous buffer)
- prefer hierarchical all-reduce for <64KB messages

perfbot: [bench-ci] tp-allreduce-microbench: ring baseline median=1.08ms p95=2.4ms; tree median=0.86ms p95=1.9ms; overall regression reduced by 14% (see artifact).

liam: nice. Did you try enabling persistent kernel fusion so compute overlaps with comm?

maria: yes, enabling persistent compute kernel reduced window where GPU is idle but didn't fully hide communication - because NCCL op itself serialized across ranks in ring. Overlap only improves when messages are bigger or we pipeline multiple micro-ops.

devin: thoughts: 1) change batching heuristic to coalesce until either latency budget hit or contiguous size >= X; 2) add an opportunistic merge task that runs inline when aggregate frag count > N; 3) switch to tree for tiny reductions.

kai: caveat - tree needs extra buffers and incurs more PCIe hops on some topologies. We need topology-aware policy: for NVLink full mesh prefer ring for >Y, else tree for <Y. Also test with asymmetric bandwidth (we saw one host with degraded NVLink) - tree gives better fan-in resilience.

maria: created a short RFC in #eng-runtime and opened a canary PR: runtime:tp/allow-hierarchical-allreduce + batching heuristics. Will run cluster canary on dedicated-2 (low traffic).

liam: ping me when canary starts. I'll watch traces and check KV cache churn.

devin: one more data point - when we compact the KV cache eviction passes into a single op, all-reduce messages size distribution shifts right and tail drops ~22%. So KV cache behavior interacts strongly.

maria: good to know. plan: 1) canary hierarchical-tree for <64KB; 2) change batching to prefer coalescing up to 128KB; 3) instrument metrics: "allreduce_frag_count", "allreduce_avg_msg_bytes", "kvcache_compact_ops".

kai: add guardrails: fall back to ring if topology report shows deep chain link or if GPU count <4.

perfbot: [canary-run] started at 1902507200 on dedicated-2. Artifacts will appear under /bench/artifacts/1902507200/

maria: thanks all. Will post follow-up with canary numbers. cc @liam @devin :rocket:
